Asha —

Appreciate the detail — attached is a quick sketch (PDF) with two tariffing approaches: 

1) Platform-first: single platform fee (annualized) + per-site operator license. Simple invoices, predictable platform revenue.
2) Node-first: per-node consumption + smaller platform fee, better for customers who want capex-aligned model.

Key notes in the doc:
- Pilot pricing: deeply discounted pilot (one-time credit of 30% off first 6 months) if they commit to a production conversion within 6 months.
- Migration credits: we can offer milestone credits tied to cutover progress (10% after staging, 15% at go-live, remainder on adoption metric).
- Support tranches: Bronze (business-hours), Silver (24x5 L2 + 4hr response), Gold (24x7 L2 + SRE retainer + 1hr P1).

Marissa — can you review the platform / operator split numbers and confirm the amortization window we typically use for pilots?
Kimberly — can you add the SLA response language we want for Gold (incidents/sec escalation)?

Diego
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Diego / Kimberly / Asha —

Quick internal check: the amortization window I used in the sketch is 36 months for platform fees when customers capitalize; operator licenses we treat as 24 months for budgeting. For pilots we typically accelerate amortization to 12 months if we provide a pilot credit so the revenue recognition is cleaner. 

I recommend we present both models to HealthLytics side-by-side: 
- Option A: Platform-first (annualized platform fee, operator licenses 24mo) — less OPEX variability, good for finance teams focused on predictable OPEX.
- Option B: Node-first (per-node + small platform fee) — aligns with capex budgets, lower upfront platform fee but higher per-node running cost.

On credits: the migration credit schedule proposed looks OK but let's tighten acceptance criteria (staging sign-off form + performance benchmark). I'll draft short acceptance wording.

Marissa
Head of Commercials
